results.title: Top juniors, rising stars set for Olivarez netfest showdown
results.description: The country’s top junior tennis talents, rising stars and promising newcomers converge beginning Thursday, Aug. 6, for what is expected to be a fierce battle for titles and valuable ranking points in the Mayor Edwin Olivarez Juniors Age Group Tennis Championships in Sucat, Parañaque. A total of 256 players will compete across eight boys’ and girls’ age-group divisions, each featuring a full 32-player draw – a rare turnout that highlights the sustained growth of junior tennis and the surge in interest generated by Alex Eala’s breakthrough success on the international stage. Leading the girls’ premier 18-and-under division are Ayl Gonzaga, Ava Banson, Jana Bermejo and Jasmine Sardona, who hope to emulate Eala’s rise. Also in the hunt are Melatiah Pascua, Agatha Asistio, Sofia Demadara and Cristina Reyes. Gonzaga, Banson, Sardona and Bermejo likewise headline the 16-and-U category, where they will be challenged by Francine Wong, fresh from a twin-title sweep in last week’s Palawan Junior Series stop in San Pablo City, Laguna. The tournament serves as the second leg of the Luzon swing of the Palawan Junior Series, which was launched nationwide earlier this year by Palawan Pawnshop president and CEO Bobby Castro following successful three-leg circuits in Mindanao and the Visayas. It also forms part of the Olivarez family’s continuing commitment to grassroots tennis development by providing young players with a high-level competitive platform. With the record turnout, organizers will utilize both the Olivarez Sports Center and the Parañaque indoor courts, with matches to be played on clay throughout the tournament. Nicholas Andala, Martin Paulsen, Anthony Cosca and Nathan Cansana spearhead the boys’ 18-and-U field, but they are expected to face stiff resistance from Vivaan Garg, Jairo Flores, Akio Kue and Bien Tulop in the Group 2 event sanctioned by Philta and Universal Tennis Ranking and presented by Dunlop. Andala, Cosca, Garg, Kue and Flores also bolster the 16-and-U division alongside Antonio Bengzon, Jan Villeno and Tyronne Caro. Villeno and Caro, meanwhile, emerge as the top seeds in the 14-and-U class, which also features Yuan Torrente, Jfsky Berille, Juan Antonio Cablitas, Djokovic Garcia, Don Simplicio Bermejo and Liam Harrow. Fresh from upsetting top seed Harrow to capture the 12-and-U title in San Pablo, Lance Recto seeks another championship but must again contend with Harrow, as well as Raven Licayan, Rafael Cablitas and Leonardo Manio III in another loaded field. In the girls’ 14-and-U division, Leanne Barrido and Wong head the favorites, although Jaynelle Castro, Talitha Lopez, Riomy Ambrad, Megumi Deura, Julia Bermejo and Arabela Barandiaran have the talent to mount serious title bids. Eilythia Comia also shoots for back-to-back girls’ 12-and-U crowns after her San Pablo triumph, with Castro, Misty May Principe, Margaret Abacan, Brielle Loyola, Abrielle Asistio, Caitleen Villacortes and Blaire Rada all eager to deny her repeat bid in the tournament backed by ICON Golf & Sports and the Palawan Group of Companies. The Luzon swing concludes on Aug. 20-30 with the Gentry Juniors at the Colegio de San Agustin Tennis Stadium in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan, before culminating with the Gentry Open. For details and registration, interested participants may contact tournament director Bobby Mangunay at 0915-404-6464.

results.title: Two young women suspected of petty theft die in Lahore police custody
results.description: LAHORE: Two young women, suspected of stealing a small amount of cash and gold jewellery from a house, later died in the police custody under mysterious circumstances here on Tuesday. The women were brought to the Township police station when a local resident accused them of stealing money and gold ornaments from his house. However, one of them was later shifted to Lytton Road police station. As per initial reports, health condition of both women worsened in police custody owing to reasons yet to be ascertained. The suspects were shifted to different hospitals, where doctors declared them “received dead,” adding to the concern of police authorities as they were already facing an odd situation following the alleged rape of a mentally challenged girl by a police official inside a police station in Ghaziabad on Tuesday. DIG claims the suspects died of drug overdose The complainant, Zeeshan Latif, alleged in the FIR that the women entered his house and asked his wife for water. He said when his wife went to fetch water, the suspects stole her gold ornaments and Rs5,000 cash from the house. He said that as the women were caught red-handed, locals gathered there, thrashed them and then handed them over to the police. A spokesperson for the investigation police late on Tuesday made it clear that the women died in the custody of the operations wing police as was evident from the call made by them (officials of the operations wing) to the Rescue 1122 to shift them to hospitals. Operations DIG Faisal Kamran told Dawn that one of the suspects fainted in Township police station, while the other in Lytton Road police station. He said both women were immediately rushed to hospitals, where they were pronounced dead by the attending doctors. To a question, he said that the Township police had lodged an FIR against the suspects around 4:50pm. He said that one of the suspects was shifted to the Lytton Road police station, to hand her over to women police officials for further investigation, while the other was still in the custody of Township police. The DIG strongly denied the allegations that the women were tortured or treated harshly in custody. “As per initial inquiry reports, both were chronic drug addicts,” Kamran said, claiming the health condition of the women was compromised due to probable drug overdose, when they were handed over to the operations police. The incident still required a high level inquiry to dig out facts as the death of two women in custody must not be ignored under any circumstances, he added. He said the police officials are in contact with the doctors of the concerned hospitals in order to get the postmortem examination of the bodies conducted as soon as possible. To another question, the DIG said the police have obtained video clips showing the women after they were caught by the area residents. He said a video recording also showed one of the women being questioned by a police official. The video shows the woman asking the policeman to arrange narcotics for her, he added. The DIG said that more details would be shared with the media once investigations into the incident are finalised. Published in Dawn, August 5th, 2026
